First comparison? Here’s the 20-second setup.
01

Bring your runs

Paste a YouTube, Twitch VOD, or X video link and press Load, or click Choose video to open a local file. Mix sources on either side. Both begin muted.

02

Line up the start

Set each start point to the same gameplay moment. Use ± seconds for big moves and ±1 frame for small adjustments. Select the video’s FPS.

03

Spot the difference

Use the play button or Space. Reset or R returns supported videos to their saved starts. The toolbar controls one supported video or both together. After clicking inside an embedded player, click outside it to use these shortcuts.

Start points range from 0:00 to 10:00; the rest of a long video is still playable. One frame means 1 ÷ your selected FPS in seconds. Embedded players may seek to nearby frames, so this is a review tool, not an exact run timer.

Ads, buffering, or different speeds can put videos out of step. For repeatable comparisons, use two recorded videos at the same speed and reset after buffering. Some videos are private, deleted, age restricted, subscriber only, or blocked from embedding by their owner.

Twitch live streams aren’t supported. For a Twitch VOD, click Play inside each player once; it will pause at your saved start and unlock the shared controls below the menus. X video posts load into a controllable video player using the public FxEmbed lookup service. Private, deleted, or non-video posts cannot be loaded. Twitch clips still use their own controls. Your settings are saved only in this browser. Local files play directly from your device and are never uploaded. After refreshing, choose those files again; their starting points and FPS are saved. Video formats and codecs must be supported by your browser. Online videos connect to their original platforms when loaded.
